# r4.3

- Speeds up repeated remote file operations by reusing the connected session's authenticated operation connection. Remote moves rename selected roots without scanning their contents and share one connection across the selection.
- Accelerates same-server copies with supported server-side copy-data, bounded overlapping small-file copies, a sliding relay-transfer window and concurrent handle closure. Server handle limits still bound concurrency; acknowledged sibling successes are retained after a partial failure, and uncertain mutations are never automatically replayed.
- Shows transferred bytes separately from completed selected items, including the current small-file group. Move progress reports completed items rather than an invented byte percentage.
- Adds remote ZIP compression and extraction. ZIP data stays on the server. Requires a Linux SSH endpoint with command execution, Python 3.8 or newer with zipfile/zlib, and libc/filesystem support for renameat2 with RENAME_NOREPLACE. SFTP-only accounts, missing capabilities and non-Linux endpoints, including Windows and macOS, are not supported.
- Remote archives use a private staging directory, verify matching SSH/SFTP namespaces and publish without overwriting an existing destination. Symlinks, special files, unsafe or ambiguous member paths, encrypted/unsupported formats and oversized archives are refused. Extraction supports stored/deflated ZIP entries; ZIP64 central-directory records are not supported.

## Limits and verification

Stop other applications changing the selected files. Copy and archive operations do not provide a filesystem snapshot against concurrent writers. Cancellation can wait for admitted requests or server cleanup. If a connection drops without a terminal result, refresh the destination before retrying; a reported .nearly-zip-* staging directory may remain for inspection.

Performance measurements use generated localhost fixtures and debug executables. Actual speed depends on latency, file sizes, storage and server capabilities; no new WinSCP comparison or real-server end-to-end ZIP qualification is claimed. Linux helper tests exercise real generated archives; Windows SSH transport tests use a fake localhost executor. Full real-server, long-duration, installation and upgrade qualification remain separate.

Stable release, replacing r4.2 as Latest. Uses the existing application registration, settings and normal updater channel. The release pipeline builds and validates the installer without installing it on the user's computer.
